clue.text: Wife has the bottle for it …

definitions.text: Wife has the bottle for it

parts.note: 'old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, so Dutch alone can stand for her
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A woman downs a drink to steel herself for some task, the ellipsis promising more to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a wife (DUTCH) has bottle (COURAGE), and the drink that supplies that nerve is the phrase itself. The ellipsis runs on into 8 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Drink-fuelled bravery is called by this phrase, so a bottle taken to nerve oneself for a deed fits it exactly.

clue.text: Bouncer spent no time sleeping

indicators.note: spent here means used up and gone, so the letter is lost from the word

parts.note: a doorman guards a club's entrance, a bouncer
O, nought, stands for no or nothing

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer took no time at all to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: One O of DOORMAN goes ('spent no'), leaving DORMAN, then T for time is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive as if asleep, as with a sleeping volcano.

clue.text: Renegade Tory regularly meeting top Conservative leaders

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters, here the first and third of Tory

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or top

indicators.note: leaders keeps only the leading letters of the word, dropping its tail

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the Conservative party

explanation.surface: A rebellious Tory keeps meeting the party's top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: TR comes from alternate letters of 'Tory', AI (A1) from 'top', and TOR from the leading letters of TORY ('Conservative leaders').
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts his cause, and so is a turncoat or betrayer.

clue.text: Busby, perhaps, has rare sporting achievements

definitions.text: Busby, perhaps, has rare sporting achievements

parts.words: Busby, perhaps, has rare sporting achievements
parts.note: a busby is a tall fur military hat, and the sporting feats are three goals or wickets in a row; also nods to Sir Matt Busby, the Manchester United manager

explanation.surface: A football manager collects some unusual sporting triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: Busby suggests Sir Matt Busby of Manchester United; it is also a bearskin-style hat, which with tricks gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-trick is three successes in a row by one player, a feat rare enough to celebrate.

clue.text: Ignoring the odd nomad, swims in watering hole

indicators.note: ignoring the odd letters keeps the even ones, running across both words

explanation.surface: A desert wanderer, leaving his companion behind, bathes at a waterhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' seems to describe a strange nomad; it means the odd-numbered letters of 'nomad swims', which are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile desert spot with water, where travellers drink.

clue.text: Men recalled an old-fashioned footballer

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are taken backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, men

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters are formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers bring back to mind a veteran player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one adjective; 'an old' is the fodder and 'fashioned' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronaldo is the name of famous Brazilian and Portuguese footballers.

clue.text: Resolute old lady takes on immature couple

parts.note: gran is an affectionate word for a grandmother, an old lady

indicators.note: immature, not fully grown, has its front missing, so the opening letters are cut away

parts.note: to couple is to join or unite

explanation.surface: A determined grandmother takes on a pair of youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAN 'takes on' (adds) UNITE cut short at its start, leaving ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is hard rock, and figuratively means unyielding or firm of purpose.

clue.text: Eighty-eight flaws to date? I will have to make some changes!

indicators.text: will have to make some changes
indicators.note: making changes says the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to errors so far and resolves to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO FAT LADIES is the traditional bingo caller's call for the number 88, the digits likened to two stout figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo calls give nicknames to numbers, and this one stands for eighty-eight.

clue.text: … and has absolute authority!

parts.note: arrant means utter or out-and-out, as in an arrant fool
arrant means utter or out-and-out, as in an arrant fool

explanation.surface: The wife from the previous clue turns out to rule the household outright.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 1 across, so the clue reads on from 'Wife': W, the usual abbreviation for wife, comes from that word, then 'and has' links it to ARRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is a document giving official authority, and the word also means the authority or justification itself.

clue.text: Footwear of commandos in foreign land? On the contrary

indicators.note: in would put the commandos inside the land, but the next phrase flips that
on the contrary says the opposite of the stated containment holds: the land goes inside the commandos

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service, its commando regiment

indicators.note: foreign suggests the word land made strange, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier's boots are queried as troops serve in some distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures soldiers abroad, but 'On the contrary' flips the stated containment: the jumbled land goes into the commandos rather than the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandals are open shoes held on by straps, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Pedestrian way reversed by solicitor

parts.note: a street is a way or road
a pedestrian is a walker

explanation.surface: A road was changed round by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian way' gives WALKER STREET; 'reversed' swaps the pair. 'solicitor' looks legal, but means one who solicits for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetwalker is a prostitute, who solicits clients in the street.

clue.text: He eats well following religious festival

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in p. 12 f.
Easter is the Christian festival of the resurrection

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a big meal after a holy day's celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A feaster is one who feasts, that is a person who dines lavishly and heartily.

clue.text: Join undercover unit as a fighter

indicators.note: undercover says one piece is concealed beneath the cover of another, placed inside it

parts.note: to solder is to join metal with fused alloy
I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit

explanation.surface: A recruit signs up to a secret squad to serve in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercover unit' looks like a spy cell, but 'undercover' puts the unit I inside SOLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a member of an army, someone who fights in wars.

clue.text: Starts to tell agriculturalists that King Edward is a local spud

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of the next three words

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: Farmers are informed that a King Edward, a British potato variety, is the regional potato.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward really is a potato variety, which makes it look like part of the definition; here it is the royal cipher ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is a dialect or colloquial word for a potato, so a regional name for one.

clue.text: Broadcast a scene not typical of Chinese city

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A television transmission shows a view said to be unrepresentative of some Chinese place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as television, but it scatters the letters of 'a scene not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese describes things belonging to Canton, the old name of Guangzhou in southern China.

clue.text: Ignorance and evil incense the church

indicators.note: evil as in bad or corrupted, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Not knowing better, and wicked perfume in a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is a formal word for lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Deals with Bill's clothes

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD for short; the 's is a link
dresses are articles of clothing

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a man named Bill's wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' seems to be a man's name; it is an advertising bill, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to tackle or deal with it.

clue.text: Dull, stolid, stupid husband

indicators.note: stupid as in muddled, so the letters are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of unflattering words describing a dim spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Doltish means stupid like a dolt, and dull can mean slow-witted.

clue.text: Believes Hampshire town is repressed

indicators.note: repressed means held down out of sight, so the answer is concealed in the words

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a southern English county town is buttoned-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hampshire town' looks like the definition, but Evesham is in Worcestershire; Hampshire supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire, England.

clue.text: Afford some original Lowrys

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A buyer can stretch to a few genuine paintings by L. S. Lowry, the English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to grant or permit, as in affording someone a chance.

clue.text: The whole of the Sun is full of celebrities

parts.note: all means the whole of something
the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: Every page of the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, is packed with famous people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid famous for celebrity coverage, which disguises the star.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast or team is made up entirely of famous performers.

clue.text: Cricketer supports sledging

parts.note: legs support a table or a body
sledging is cricket slang for verbally abusing a batsman; lip is cheeky insolent talk

explanation.surface: A cricket player backs the taunting of opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg slip is a fielding position close behind the batsman on the leg side, and so the fielder there.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg slip names a fielding position, used for the player who fields there.

clue.text: Quiet holy man eradicated disease

indicators.note: eradicated means rooted out, so the holy man's letters are removed

parts.note: quiet as a noun means calm or stillness
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A peaceful saint wiped out a plague.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ST from the front of STILLNESS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Illness and disease are synonyms for being unwell.

clue.text: Sorry to dishearten Hindu holy man

parts.note: sorry can mean sad or pitiable

indicators.note: dishearten here means take the heart out, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: It is regrettable to discourage a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic, a wandering holy man.

clue.text: Unlawful 21 executed by getting rid of senator from an African state

parts.note: 21 across, a disease, can also be called an ill

indicators.note: getting rid of says letters are thrown out of the word that follows

parts.note: Senegal is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A sickness carried out by expelling a politician from a nation in Africa is criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to 21 across; ILL is used as a noun for an illness. 'executed by' is link material. Dropping SEN from SENEGAL leaves EGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal and unlawful both mean forbidden by law.

clue.text: A quarter wanted to be flogged

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
wanted means desired or wished

explanation.surface: Someone longed for a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To swish someone is to beat them with a cane, the cane making a swishing sound.

clue.text: Finally run a story about me and a girl

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word run
about says the story wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a tale is a story
I is how the speaker refers to me

explanation.surface: A tale ends up being told about the writer and a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is a girl's name; names are often defined by girl or boy.

clue.text: Jerry's least favourite play?

parts.note: Jerry is the cartoon mouse of Tom and Jerry, and the stage play he would hate is the long-running Agatha Christie whodunit named after a rodent snare

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer's dislikes are guessed at.
explanation.walkthrough: The Agatha Christie play has run in London since 1952; a mouse would fear its title most.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Christie's play, and literally a device for catching mice, which Jerry would loathe.
